'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''

**The [[Somali National Army|army]] reports the killing of 27 [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] [[jihadist]]s near [[Awdheegle]], [[Lower Shabelle]], along with the destruction of [[militant]] hideouts, as part of an ongoing campaign to secure areas previously under al-Shabaab control. '''Disasters and accidents'''
*Three [[Ukrainian Air Force]] pilots are killed when two [[Aero L-39 Albatros|L-39 trainer aircraft]] collide in midair in [[Zhytomyr]], [[Ukraine]]. [[Andrii Pilshchykov]] was among the dead. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/8/26/russia-ukraine-war-live-ukrainian-commander-hails-breakthrough-in-south (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/aug/27/ukrainian-pilot-juice-among-three-killed-in-jet-collision-says-volodymyr-zelenskiy (''The Guardian'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[British Museum]] [[List of directors of the British Museum|director]] [[Hartwig Fischer]] resigns after insufficient investigations of recent [[British Museum#Thefts|thefts]] of items from the museum's collection, including [[jewelry]] and [[antiquities]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/uk/2023/0825/1401707-british-museum (AFP via RTÉ)] [https://apnews.com/article/british-museum-thefts-director-resigns-hartwig-fischer-b2de328dc2acb0dd90ef7eceb4897533 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022–2023 food crises]]
**[[Norway]] announces that it will spend 63 million [[Norwegian krone|kroner]] ([[US$]]6 million) each year on [[grain]] reserves due to [[Environmentalism|environmental]] and [[geopolitical]] concerns. [https://apnews.com/article/norway-emergency-stockpile-grain-seed-vault-3646588adf68c08d8b0b101758efed40 (AP)]
*[[Haitian crisis (2018–present)|Haitian crisis]]
**Two telecommunication companies in [[Haiti]], [[Digicel]] and Access Haiti, said their [[fiber optic cables]] were severed this week, temporarily disrupting service in suspected acts of [[sabotage]] by criminal gangs. [https://apnews.com/article/haiti-digicel-gangs-cables-cut-fcce6d69803d59d6b19ea02f98f5e296 (AP)]
*The [[United Auto Workers]] of the [[Automotive industry in the United States|United States]] vote to call a [[Strike action|strike]] if [[Collective bargaining|contract negotiations]] with [[Ford Motor Company|Ford]], [[General Motors]], and [[Stellantis]] are not finalized by the stated deadline. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20230825-possible-us-auto-strike-as-unions-flex-muscle-in-hot-labor-summer (AFP via RFI)]
*A [[U.S.]] [[Federal government of the United States|federal]] control board files a new plan for [[restructuring]] $10 billion in [[debt]] owned by [[Puerto Rico]]’s [[LUMA Energy|power company]] in an attempt to end [[bankruptcy]] negotiations. [https://apnews.com/article/puerto-rico-power-company-debt-restructuring-c10aafb2e375c577dce57003e91cb41b (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 12 people are killed and 80 are injured in a [[human crush]] during the opening ceremony of the [[Indian Ocean Island Games]] at the [[Mahamasina Municipal Stadium]] in [[Antananarivo]], [[Madagascar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/stampede-madagascars-national-stadium-kills-12-injures-around-80-pm-2023-08-25/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2023 Nigerien crisis]]
**[[Foreign relations of Niger]]
***The ruling [[Niger]]ien [[National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland|military junta]] orders the [[ambassador]]s of [[France]], [[Germany]], [[Nigeria]], and the United States to [[Persona non grata|leave]] the country. France rejects the ultimatum, claiming they do not recognize its authority, while the US claims it has received no request to withdraw its personnel from Niger. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/niger-gives-us-ambassador-48-hours-leave-country-afp-2023-08-25/ (Reuters)] [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/africa/article/3232382/niger-junta-asks-french-ambassador-leave-country (AFP via ''SCMP'')] 
*[[Finland–Russia relations]]
**[[Yan Petrovsky]], one of the leaders of the [[Russia|Russian]] [[far-right]] [[paramilitary]] [[Rusich Group]], is detained in [[Finland]]. [[Ukraine]] has sent a request for Petrovsky's [[extradition]]. [https://meduza.io/news/2023/08/25/v-finlyandii-zaderzhan-odin-iz-liderov-dshrg-rusich-yan-petrovskiy-kotorogo-ukraina-obvinyaet-v-prestupleniyah-v-donbasse (Meduza)] [https://www.fontanka.ru/2023/08/25/72640268/ (Fontanka.ru)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in the United States]]
**[[Capital punishment in Alabama]]
***The [[Alabama]] [[Attorney General of Alabama|attorney general]]’s office makes a filing with the [[Supreme Court of Alabama]] indicating plans to carry out a death penalty by [[nitrogen hypoxia]], an [[execution]] method that is authorized in three US states but has never been used. [https://apnews.com/article/alabama-death-penalty-nitrogen-hypoxia-a6f414ff6147cbd38de6a8cd01f96653 (AP)]
*[[Corruption in Lebanon]]
**[[Monaco]]’s judicial authorities announce they have closed a probe against [[Lebanon]]’s caretaker [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|prime minister]] [[Najib Mikati]] and his family over [[corruption]] allegations due to lack of evidence. [https://apnews.com/article/lebanon-najib-mikati-monaco-corruption-1c9564cb8071163d688156f611c2c78d (AP)]
*[[Homelessness in the United States]]
**Officials in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]], announce [[Boston Police Department|police]] will remove tents and other makeshift shelters at the [[Mass and Cass]] [[tent city]], an encampment for the homeless, many of whom struggle with [[mental health]] issues and [[substance abuse]] disorders. [https://apnews.com/article/homelessness-boston-tent-encampment-d59d3739910566f96d50d72e2ad476c0 (AP)]
*[[Yale University]] and a student group announce they have reached a settlement in a [[United States federal courts|U.S. federal]] [[lawsuit]] that accused the [[Ivy League]] school of [[discriminating]] against students with [[mental health]] [[disabilities]], including pressuring them to withdraw. [https://apnews.com/article/yale-students-mental-health-discrimination-lawsuit-settlement-b444590c2c1982aca3ee848c2ec535b4 (AP)]
*A [[Pakistani Americans|Pakistani]] doctor and former [[Mayo Clinic]] research coordinator who sought to join the [[Islamic State]] [[terrorist]] group to fight in [[Syria]] and expressed interest in carrying out attacks in the U.S. is [[sentence (law)|sentenced]] to 18 years in prison. [https://apnews.com/article/islamic-state-terrorism-minnesota-0e4a09840bed202cac17e18e3dfd87d5 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Aftermath of the Afghanistan War (2001–2021)|Aftermath of the Afghanistan War]]
**[[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Rep.]] [[Cory Mills]] introduces articles for [[impeachment]] against [[United States Secretary of Defense|Defense Secretary]] [[Lloyd Austin]], accusing Austin of ignoring key intelligence during [[2020–2021 U.S. troop withdrawal from Afghanistan|the withdrawal]] of [[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] from [[Afghanistan]] that caused [[2021 Kabul airport attack|the killing of 13 soldiers]] and the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|surrender]] of [[Kabul]] to the [[Taliban]]. **[[Sandra Torres]], who lost [[Guatemala]]'s [[President of Guatemala|presidential]] election, files a complaint alleging [[Electoral fraud|fraud in the way the votes were counted]]. [https://apnews.com/article/guatemala-sandra-torres-election-voter-fraud-888e42a2c17d11483926ee89c42d1e93 (AP)]
